'''Biswa Ranjan Nag''' (1 October 1932 – 6 April 2004) was an Indian physicist and the [[Sisir Kumar Mitra]] chair professor at [[Rajabazar Science College]], [[University of Calcutta]]. Known for his research in [[semiconductor physics]], Nag was an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards for his contributions to Physical Sciences in 1974.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx |title=View Bhatnagar Awardees |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |date=2016 |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link – please select award year to see details}}

== Biography ==
[[File:The Calcutta University by Francis Frith.jpg|thumb|220px|upright=1|left|Nag completed his master's degree and served as faculty in the [[University of Calcutta]]'s Institute of Radiophysics and Electronics (IRE).]]
Born on 1 October 1932 to Sailabala and Satyaranjan Nag at [[Comilla]], a city along the [[Dhaka-Chittagong Highway]] in the undivided [[Bengal]] of the [[British India]] (presently in Bangladesh), B. R. Nag did his graduate studies at [[Presidency College, Calcutta]], during 1949–51 and earned a master's degree in technology (M.Tech.) from the Institute of Radiophysics and Electronics (IRE) at the [[Rajabazar Science College]] campus of the [[University of Calcutta]] in 1954.<ref name="B. R. Nag - Obituary">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iisc.ernet.in/currsci/jun102004/1565.pdf |title=B. R. Nag – Obituary |date=2004 |publisher=Current Science}}</ref> He started his career in 1956 as a faculty member at IRE and simultaneously pursued doctoral studies, mentored by Arun K. Choudhury. In between, he spent one year at the [[University of Wisconsin]], obtaining an MS in 1959.  Mr. Nag returned to Calcutta to resume his doctoral work, and earned his PhD in 1961. Continuing his teaching career, he became a full professor in 1968.<ref name="Proceedings of the International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication">{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YcJv1XzIWSMC&pg=PR19 |title=Proceedings of the International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication |publisher=Allied Publishers |year=1998 |isbn=978-81-7023-767-9 |pages=19–}}</ref> Further research earned him a [[Doctor of Science]] degree from Calcutta University in 1972.<ref name="Deceased fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N78-0496 |title=Deceased fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=26 April 2017 |archive-date=7 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807153331/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N78-0496 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He served out his regular academic career at the university and continued his association past his superannuation in 1997 as its Sisir Kumar Mitra professor.<ref name="Codec History">{{Cite web |url=http://www.codec-rpe.org/codechistory.html |title=Codec History |date=2017 |publisher=CODEC 2012}}</ref> In between, he also served as a Commonwealth visiting professor at [[Bangor, Gwynedd]].<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

Nag was married to Mridula Roy Choudhury, and the couple had two children, Biswadeep and Mriduchanda. He died on 6 April 2004 in Kolkata, at the age of 71.<ref name="B. R. Nag - Obituary" />

== Legacy ==
[[File:Silicon.jpg|thumb|200px|[[Silicon]] crystals, a common semiconducting material]]
Nag's work focused on semiconductors, and it helped in widening our understanding of the electrical [[transport phenomena]] in those high [[electrical resistance|electrical resistant]] solids.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=322 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize}}</ref> During his early years at Calcutta University, he led a group of students who were engaged in the studies on microwave measurements of semiconductor properties and did advanced research on [[Gunn effect]] and [[microwave radiation]].<ref name="B. R. Nag - Obituary" /> He demonstrated the temperature independence of [[two-dimensional electron gas]] and its ''alloy scattering limited mobility'' which was a first time discovery.<ref name="Deceased fellow" /><ref name="Alloy scattering limited mobility of two-dimensional electron gas formed in In0.53Ga0.47As">{{Cite journal |last=P.K. Basu, B.R. Nag |title=Alloy scattering limited mobility of two-dimensional electron gas formed in In0.53Ga0.47As |journal=Surface Science |date=1984 |volume=142 |issue=1–3 |pages=256–259 |doi=10.1016/0039-6028(84)90317-0 |bibcode=1984SurSc.142..256B}}</ref> His studies revealed the non-parabolic nature of electron energy dispersion in narrow [[quantum well]]s, and this modified the theory of ''interface roughness scattering limited mobility for Quantum Wells with finite barrier height and Well width''. [[Epitaxy#Liquid-phase|Liquid phase Epitaxy]] Semiconducting III–V compounds, [[acousto-electric effect]] and free carrier absorption, [[Gini ratio]] and [[Coefficient of thermal expansion|Si coefficient]] related to hot-electron galvanomagnetic transport were some of the other areas of his research.<ref name="B. R. Nag - Obituary" /> He contributed to the development of electron transport theory related to semiconductors and developed a [[Monte Carlo method]] for the computation of coefficients related to velocity correlation, diffusion and noise parameters.<ref name="Proceedings of the International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication" /> His body of work is reported to have relevance to the fields of [[microwave communications]] and [[radar]], especially in the development of microwave semiconductor devices.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web |url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |date=1999 |access-date=14 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and the article repository of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] has listed 190 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Nag=3ABiswaranjan=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He authored three monographs, ''Theory of electrical transport in semiconductors'',<ref name="Nag1972">{{cite book |author=B. R. Nag |title=Theory of electrical transport in semiconductors |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=peANAQAAIAAJ |year=1972 |publisher=Pergamon Press |isbn=9780080168029}}</ref> ''Physics of Quantum Well Devices''<ref name="Nag2006">{{cite book |author=B.R. Nag |title=Physics of Quantum Well Devices |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=797pBwAAQBAJ |date=11 April 2006 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-0-306-47127-8}}</ref> and ''Electron Transport in Compound Semiconductors''<ref name="Nag2012">{{cite book |author=B.R. Nag |title=Electron Transport in Compound Semiconductors |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Nq3oCAAAQBAJ |date=6 December 2012 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-642-81416-7}}</ref> of which the last mentioned is reported to be a significant reference text for researchers.<ref name="B. R. Nag - Obituary" /> He also contributed chapters to books published by others<ref name="(India)1968">{{cite book |author=Institution of Engineers (India) |title=Journal of the Institution of Engineers (India) |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVBQAAAAYAAJ |date=July 1968 |publisher=The Institution}}</ref><ref name="Lal2012">{{cite book |author=K. Lal |title=Synthesis, Crystal Growth and Characterization |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1f14AAAAQBAJ&pg=PA426 |date=2 December 2012 |publisher=Elsevier Science |isbn=978-0-08-098469-8 |pages=426–}}</ref><ref name="Division1967">{{cite book |author=Institution of Engineers (India). Metallurgy & Material Science Division |title=Journal of the Institution of Engineers (India). Part MM, Mining & Metallurgy Division |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bz4nAQAAMAAJ |year=1967 |publisher=The Institution}}</ref> and his work has drawn citations in a number of books.<ref name="Nalwa2001">{{cite book |author=Hari Singh Nalwa |title=Handbook of Thin Films, Five-Volume Set |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r-WzXVaKctIC&pg=PA492 |date=17 November 2001 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-08-053324-7 |pages=492–}}</ref><ref name="Böer2014">{{cite book |author=Karl W. Böer |title=Handbook of the Physics of Thin-Film Solar Cells |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Cki3BAAAQBAJ&pg=PA826 |date=23 April 2014 |publisher=Springer Science & Business |isbn=978-3-642-36748-9 |pages=826–}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Proceedings of the International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YcJv1XzIWSMC&pg=PA19 |year=1998 |publisher=Allied Publishers |isbn=978-81-7023-767-9 |pages=19–}}</ref><ref name="GhatakBhattacharya2014">{{cite book |author1=Kamakhya P. Ghatak |author2=Sitangshu Bhattacharya |title=Heavily-Doped 2D-Quantized Structures and the Einstein Relation |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fVIqBAAAQBAJ&pg=PR17 |date=30 July 2014 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-08380-3 |pages=17–}}</ref><ref name="GhatakBhattacharya2008">{{cite book |author1=Kamakhya Prasad Ghatak |author2=Sitangshu Bhattacharya |author3=Debashis De |title=Einstein Relation in Compound Semiconductors and Their Nanostructures |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wfEVLbxwUjcC&pg=PA9 |date=16 November 2008 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-540-79557-5 |pages=9–}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Nag, a founder fellow of the [[Indian National Academy of Engineering]],<ref name="B. R. Nag - Obituary" /> received the J. C. Bose Memorial Prize of the [[British Institution of Radio Engineers]] in 1964.<ref name="Proceedings of the International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication" /> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1974.<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |title=CSIR list of Awardees |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref> He was selected for the [[Jawaharlal Nehru Fellowship]] in 1975,<ref name="List of Jawaharlal Nehru Fellows">{{Cite web |url=https://www.jnmf.in/flist.html |title=List of Jawaharlal Nehru Fellows |date=2017 |publisher=Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Fund}}</ref> and the [[Indian National Science Academy]] elected him as a fellow in 1978;<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=14 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> the academy would honor him again in 1993 with the INSA Prize for Materials Science.<ref name="INSA Prize for Materials Science">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#mete |title=INSA Prize for Materials Science |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=14 April 2017 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#mete |url-status=dead}}</ref> He became an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Nag,_Prof._Biswaranjan |title=Fellow profile |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> The department of radio physics and electronics of the University of Calcutta instituted an annual conference, ''International Conference on Computers and devices for Communication (CODEC)'', in his honor in 1998, a year after Nag retired from academic service.<ref name="Codec History" />
